justification: Two correctness gates added to the (still-unwired) Housing-SEPP eligibility engine, found by a pre-wiring live sweep: heritage land was not excluded from the LMR reforms, and manor_house (a dataset gap with no min lot size) passed every lot gate. Both would have caused over-reports once the engine is wired into the live capacity ceiling. No live impact yet (engine unwired); standard tier with full unit coverage.

pre_impl.existing_data: housing_sepp_standards rows per development_type. The manor_house row has max_fsr/max_height/deep-soil/landscaping but NO min_lot_size and requires_lmr_area=False (confirmed by direct query) — a genuine dataset gap, since manor houses do have a minimum lot in the SEPP.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The engine assumed a form with no min_lot_size simply has no lot gate (true for TOD-gated R3/R4 flats) — but for manor_house that is a missing standard, not the absence of one, so it passed on any lot. Separately, the engine assumed the 776 exclusion map captures all LMR exclusions, but it does not catch heritage items/HCAs.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new file, no new data. evaluate_eligibility gains a heritage flag (suppresses requires_lmr_area forms on heritage land) and a conservative data-gap guard (a non-base, non-TOD-gated form with min_lot_size missing is ineligible). Verified by re-running the live sweep: manor_house no longer eligible anywhere; Haberfield heritage shows only base forms.

functions.name: evaluate_eligibility
functions.input: zone code, lot area and width, lat, lng, a heritage flag, and optional pre-fetched gate inputs
functions.output: a list of per-development-type FormEligibility with the heritage and lot-gap gates now applied
functions.if_none: a non-residential zone or an unavailable standards table still returns an empty list, fail-safe to base controls

values: N/A - no regulatory values are hardcoded. The heritage flag is supplied by the caller from its heritage detection; thresholds remain read from housing_sepp_standards; the new guard only withholds a form when its lot standard is absent.

queries.purpose: fetch all Housing-SEPP standards (forms, thresholds, applicable zones, LMR flag) for grouping in Python
queries.where_clause: none required — the whole small curated reference table is read and grouped in memory, not filtered per property
queries.if_0_rows: evaluate_eligibility returns an empty list so the caller keeps the base planning controls (fail-safe)
queries.if_wrong_rows: N/A — it reads the entire reference table, so there is no per-property WHERE that could select wrong rows

break_it.scenario: A heritage conservation-area lot that is in a Low and Mid-Rise reform area on the 776 map
break_it.what_happens: Without a heritage gate the engine would mark LMR flats and terraces eligible on heritage land
break_it.how: the heritage flag marks every requires_lmr_area form ineligible with a heritage reason while leaving base forms (dual occ, secondary) untouched

break_it.scenario: A small or narrow lot where manor_house has no minimum lot size in the dataset
break_it.what_happens: manor_house passed every lot gate and would inflate the ceiling on tiny lots everywhere
break_it.how: a non-base, non-TOD-gated form with a missing min_lot_size is now marked ineligible with a 'not in the dataset' reason

break_it.scenario: A legitimate R3/R4 residential flat that has no minimum lot size because it is TOD-gated by design
break_it.what_happens: An over-broad data-gap guard could wrongly withhold the valid mid-rise flat uplift in a TOD catchment
break_it.how: the guard explicitly exempts residential_flat_r3r4 forms, so they stay eligible when in a TOD catchment

break_it.scenario: The housing_sepp_standards reference query fails because the database is unreachable or times out
break_it.what_happens: An unhandled error would raise and break whatever consumes the engine
break_it.how: evaluate_eligibility wraps the standards fetch in try/except and returns an empty list so the caller keeps base controls

post_merge.manual_verify: Still unwired. The manor_house dataset gap (missing min_lot_size, questionable requires_lmr_area=False) should be corrected in housing_sepp_standards separately; until then the conservative guard withholds it. Next: P2b wires the brief ceiling to the densest ELIGIBLE form; P3 migrates the LEP/SEPP tab.
